validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, real and well-documented. This row is Enterprise Products Partners' May 31, 2023 compression-only capacity expansion of its Acadian Haynesville Extension pipeline (part of the Acadian Gas Pipeline System), adding ~400 MMcf/d of Haynesville takeaway capacity and raising total system capacity from ~2.1 Bcf/d to 2.5 Bcf/d. Confirmed via: (1) Enterprise's own May 31 2023 press release (posted on ir.enterpriseproducts.com, distributed via Businesswire, and restated on the company's 'Our History' timeline page) -- the row's existing current_ref; (2) Oil & Gas Journal, 'EPP completes 400-MMcfd Acadian Haynesville Extension expansion' (Christopher E. Smith, May 31 2023), an independently bylined trade-press writeup; (3) EIA's own 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' historical workbook (EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx), which carries a distinct row: Project Name 'Acadian Haynesville Extension', Operator 'Enterprise Products Partners', Project Type 'Expansion', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2023-05-31, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 400, State(s) LA -- a federal dataset independent of the company's own announcement, and NOT traceable to GEM. Tier: high (2+ independent origins: company disclosure vs. EIA's federal compilation; OGJ trade press as a third angle). LIVENESS: the sheet's existing current_ref (ir.enterpriseproducts.com) now 403s/times out to scripted clients -- confirmed this is a bot-wall, not a dead page (curl with a browser UA also gets 403, but the page IS live and unchanged per its Wayback capture, which passes verification with the pipeline name and '400' both present). Per standing rule this is NOT a deletion -- add the Wayback snapshot (http://web.archive.org/web/20260505074448/https://ir.enterpriseproducts.com/news-releases/news-release-details/enterprise-completes-expansion-acadian-haynesville-extension) alongside the existing ref, do not replace it. Same finding for the wiki-cited Businesswire mirror of the same release (also 403 direct, Wayback at http://web.archive.org/web/20260213033426/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20230531005287/en/Enterprise-Completes-Expansion-of-Acadian-Haynesville-Extension passes). CLASSIFICATION: correct. The press release explicitly states 'The expansion project added compression, increasing total natural gas transportation capacity ... from approximately 2.1 Bcf/d to 2.5 Bcf/d' -- no new linear pipe was built, so GEM's LengthKnown=0/Diameter=blank for this row is the CORRECT encoding per the no-new-physical-pipe rule, not a gap. PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are both correct for this high-diameter intrastate mainline capacity addition. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate. The Acadian family in this roster is four distinct, correctly-separated GEM rows for the same corridor, exactly as flagged in the task brief: P0143 (the legacy ~1,000-mile South Louisiana Acadian system predating the Haynesville extension), P3283 (the ~80-mile Gillis Lateral, proposed Sep. 2019 per the wiki-cited Pipeline & Gas Journal article -- via Wayback since the live pgjonline.com URL now 404s -- and completed 4Q2021 per Aegis Hedging's Dec. 2021 'Two Haynesville-area pipeline projects due in 2021' insight, both describing an 80-mile/1 Bcf/d lateral matching P3283's len=83/cap=1000 roster values), P5709 (the original 2011 Haynesville Extension mainline build -- 270 mi, dia 30/36/42, cap 1800 MMcf/d, matching EIA's separate 2011 'New Pipeline' row for 'Acadian Haynesville Extension' almost exactly), and P5401 (this row: the 2023 compression-only capacity expansion of that same P5709 mainline, correctly logged as its own zero-length expansion phase, the same pattern GEM uses for the Florida Gas Transmission phases). No merge is warranted. Opened and read to exhaustion: the Enterprise IR/Businesswire press release (twice, direct + Wayback), Enterprise's 'Our History' timeline page (restates the same May 2023 announcement verbatim, no new facts), the OGJ article, the EIA historical projects workbook (all Acadian-named rows), the wiki-cited 2019 PGJ article and the Aegis Hedging insight (both found to describe P3283, not this row -- see cross_row_leads), and attempted the wiki-cited mergr.com / 2010 SEC filing / bit.ly / job-posting citations, which are 2000-2010 ownership-history citations irrelevant to this 2023 row. 6 of 15 wiki-harvested citations for the Acadian page were opened; the remainder (mergr.com acquisition note, 2000 bit.ly release, 2010 SEC investor deck, two job-posting citations, and the enterprise system-map citation) concern corporate history/ownership pre-dating this expansion or are non-substantive and were not pursued further.

validity.researcher_notes: Caution for future work on this row, not a live defect (both fields are currently blank on the sheet, so nothing needs correcting today). EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook carries a row for this exact project (Completed Date 2023-05-31, Additional Capacity 400 MMcf/d -- matches) but its 'Cost (millions)' field shows 3800 and its 'Miles' field shows 275. Both are misleading if lifted directly: (a) the press release states this expansion is 'the first of $3.8 billion of organic growth capital projects' scheduled to complete in 2023 across MULTIPLE Enterprise projects (PDH 2, NGL fractionator 12, Poseidon, Mentone II, Texas Western Products) -- EIA appears to have attached that company-wide 2023 capex total to this one project row, not a project-specific cost; no source anywhere states a segment-specific dollar figure for just this compression expansion. (b) 'Miles: 275' on this expansion row is suspiciously close to the ~270 miles of the ORIGINAL Haynesville Extension mainline (P5709, confirmed via EIA's separate 2011 'New Pipeline' row and matching the roster's P5709 len=270) -- i.e. it reads as the system's total mileage restated on the expansion row, not new pipe, which directly contradicts the press release's explicit 'added compression' (no new linear pipe) language. This is exactly the aggregate-vs-segment trap the sweep SOP warns about. Recommend: leave SegmentCost UNRESOLVED and keep LengthKnown=0 as-is; do not use the EIA workbook's Cost/Miles columns for this row if pasting from it in the future.

cross_row_leads.facts: Gillis Lateral: proposed/announced Sep. 20, 2019 (Pipeline & Gas Journal); 80-mile, 1 Bcf/d intrastate lateral originating near Cheneyville, LA on the Acadian Haynesville Extension, terminating at third-party interconnects near Gillis, LA; paired with a Mansfield compressor-station (De Soto Parish) upgrade that raises the mainline's own capacity by 300 MMcf/d (1.8 to 2.1 Bcf/d); expected in service mid-2021. Matches roster P3283 (len=83, cap=1000) closely. Note: the live pgjonline.com URL for this article now 404s -- only the Wayback capture is usable.

Gillis Lateral in service (Dec. 16, 2021 article): ~80-mile pipeline from near Alexandria, LA on the Acadian Haynesville Extension to Gillis, LA interconnects; ~1 Bcf/d capacity; commercial service started via a Mansfield compressor-station (De Soto Parish) horsepower increase, raising the Acadian Haynesville Extension's own capacity from 1.8 to 2.1 Bcf/d. Confirms the P3283 in-service timing and the 1.8-to-2.1-Bcf/d step that immediately preceded this row's (P5401's) further 2.1-to-2.5-Bcf/d step in 2023.

EIA's historical projects workbook carries a separate 2011 row: 'Acadian Haynesville Extension', Enterprise Products Partners, Project Type 'New Pipeline', Completed 2011-11-01, Cost $1,500M, 270 miles, Additional Capacity 1800 MMcf/d, Diameter '30, 36, 42' in, Intrastate/State authority. Matches roster P5709 (len=270, dia=30/36/42, cap=1800) closely -- this is the original mainline build P5401 later expanded via compression.

Enterprise's own history timeline (2009 entry): unitholders approved the Duncan Energy/Acadian Gas LLC joint plan on Oct. 23, 2009 to extend the existing ~1,000-mile South Louisiana Acadian system into northwest Louisiana's Haynesville Shale via a 249-mile, 36-inch-and-30-inch pipeline with capacity up to 1.4 Bcf/d, connecting to the affiliated Cypress Gas Pipeline. Gives a 2009 proposal date and an earlier (249 mi/1.4 Bcf/d) planned scope for what became the 270-mi/1800-MMcf/d P5709 build; useful for P5709's ProposalYear.
